newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Americans boost 1996 Hungarian tourism figures.
newsitem.headline: Americans boost 1996 Hungarian tourism figures.

text.p: American guests spent 39 percent more "tourist nights" in commercial accommodation in the January-November period of 1996 in Hungary, Hungary's central statistical office (KSH) said on Monday.
The Americans were followed by the Polish who spent 36 percent more "tourist nights" and the Japanese with 29 percent, KSH said in a statement.
"More people may have been visiting American soldiers stationed in Hungary...while tourism from Japan has been growing for years," a KSH official told Reuters.
Hungary hosts thousands of U.S. troops at the U.S. Army's forward base for its IFOR/SFOR peace implementation force for Bosnia at Taszar in southern Hungary.

The total number of foreign guests staying in commercial accommodation in Hungary rose two percent, while the number of "tourist nights" foreigners spent in the country rose five percent in the first eleven months of 1996, the statement said.

In November alone, a total of 3.3 million foreigners visited Hungary, making a 19 percent rise on a year-on-year basis. In the January-November period a total of 36.8 million foreigners visited Hungary.
In the first eleven months of 1996 a total of 11.2 million Hungarians took trips abroad, nine percent down on last year's figures.
